items.summary: Maritime security sources told Reuters Oct 14 that the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride (2,824 TEU) has SUNK after a projectile strike; Pakistan's Hydrographer issued an Oct 14 navigational warning noting the sunken vessel and floating containers. It is the second vessel lost since the war began Feb 28, per IMO data; Singapore's MPA confirmed all 21 crew were safely evacuated. The same sources report the Antigua & Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao — struck Sep 23 — is also sinking after a failed rescue attempt, per Vanguard. This upgrades this morning's unconfirmed IRGC mine claim (alerted 09:40Z): the IRGC claimed the ship hit a mine on an 'unauthorised route,' but independent sources attribute the loss to a projectile strike.
items.title: GFS Pride confirmed sunk near Hormuz — second vessel lost since war began; Cape Dao also sinking

items.summary: Tuesday Oct 13 saw FOUR ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz — not the two previously reported. AFP reports a British maritime agency logged two more vessels struck Tuesday by unknown projectiles with minor damage. SeaTrade Maritime (Vanguard Tech IDs): UKMTO issued four new warnings for Oct 13 covering container ships GFS Pride, GFS Giselle and Al Saadiyat plus tanker Alfonso. GFS Giselle took minor damage but continued, all 22 crew safe (MPA confirmed); Al Saadiyat suffered no significant damage or casualties on an outbound transit; Alfonso's status is unclear — it is on Iran's PGSA non-compliance blacklist. UKMTO's October tally is now 24 warnings plus 3 advisories.
items.title: Tuesday saw four Hormuz ship attacks, not two; vessels identified, UKMTO Oct tally hits 24
